subject: Oakbridge partnership — onboarding credits, tiered revenue share & attribution model
messages:

Subject: Partnership: Oakbridge resell vs referral — quick Qs

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Oakbridge liked the latency profile and the private deployment options. Before we loop in procurement, two quick questions on the commercials so we can set expectations internally:

1) For the reseller path, do you offer a graduated revenue-share that increases with ARR thresholds, or is it a flat percent?
2) For referral credits, what's your lead registration window and how do you handle multi-touch attribution (first-touch vs demo-first)?
3) Are onboarding credits (free trial or platform credits) refundable/recoupable if the customer churns within the first 60/90 days?

We have a handful of managed-service partners who bundle software + services — we need clarity on whether commissions apply to software-only ARR or the full bundle.

Can you send a short Mutual Action Plan and a sample pricing schedule so we can share internally?

Best,
Sophie Park

Sophie.Park@oakbridge.com
+1 415-555-0193

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@oakbridge.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-07T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Partnership: Oakbridge resell vs referral — quick Qs

Hi Sophie — great to hear Oakbridge is interested. High level answers below and I attached a one-page Mutual Action Plan and a draft pricing schedule for the two paths you asked about. Attachments: Oakbridge_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx, Referral_Pricing_Schedule.pdf

Summary answers:
- Reseller (recommended for ISVs who want to resell directly): we offer a graduated rev-share tied to net ARR bands: 10% for first $0–250k, 15% for $250–1M, 20% for >$1M. There is a 12-month lookback for accelerators that triggers at the quarter boundary.
- Referral: flat 8% for the first 12 months of invoiced ARR (software-only). Lead registration window is 180 days from first qualified contact submission.
- Attribution: default is demo-first attribution (the partner that sponsors a prescriptive demo and leads the technical engagement gets attribution). We can make exceptions (e.g., first-touch) with an explicit dispute window and audit evidence.
- Onboarding credits: we offer time-limited onboarding credits that are recoverable via clawback if the customer cancels within 90 days and we were billed a credit. We have a 90-day clawback window and a pro-rata recoupment clause in the contract.
- Bundles / managed services: commission is paid on software-only ARR by default. If Oakbridge wants to be paid on bundled revenue we need an explicit carve-in and a lower rev-share multiplier (policy: bundle multiplier <= 0.6x software rate) and a disclosure in the deal registration form.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — it includes timelines, milestone owners, and sample activation credits.
2) If this aligns, legal can exchange an MSA + SOW (I've attached a short MSA draft).
3) Finance will confirm invoicing cadence and sample waterfall (ben_cc'd).

Camila — curious if you want to flag any legal/ops constraints off the bat?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to finalize.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

On Wed, Mar 7, 2028 at 11:02 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Camila — curious if you want to flag any legal/ops constraints off the bat?

Thanks Marissa — a few items from Legal/Partner Ops we should lock before commitment:

1) Clawback mechanics: we prefer the 90-day recoupment but need to define calculation: net of refunds and credits, pro-rata on recognized revenue, and not gross billings. Also specify whether onboarding credits are recorded as contra-revenue vs prepaid expense (ops will push contra-revenue).
2) Lead registration guardrails: we require a minimum lead form with qualifying fields, a single contact snapshot (email + company domain), and a 10-business-day review window. During review the lead is held in 'pending' status.
3) Double-credit protection: if a lead is registered by multiple partners, we use demo-first plus evidence-based arbitration (screenshare logs, signed SOW, or presales notes).
4) Exclusivity: Oakbridge asked about account exclusivity for 30 days on registered named accounts. Legal will permit limited exclusivity for named account registrations only if Oakbridge commits to a minimum introduction cadence and scopes out assigned named accounts in the MAP.

I attached the MSA_Draft.docx for your reference — it's a slim MSA (standard data residency, audit rights, and 90-day cancellation clawback language).

If Oakbridge wants the bundle to be commissionable (not just software), we need them to provide itemized billing (software vs services) for audit and a reduced rev-share as Marissa noted.

Camila Reyes
Sr. Partner Counsel | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

Looping in finance notes so procurement at Oakbridge has the answers they need.

Sophie — a few operational clarifications from our side:
- Invoicing cadence: Redwood invoices monthly in arrears for hosted/usage; for Dedicated we invoice at milestone or quarterly depending on contract. For rev-share payouts we do quarterly settlements with a 45-day payout window post-quarter close.
- Sample waterfall: we need to confirm whether Oakbridge will accept software-only ARR as the base for the calculation (Marissa suggested that). If yes, we apply the graduated rates on net recognized ARR.
- Reporting: Partners must submit a monthly partner report (CSV) with registered leads and closed deal references. We provide a simple template.
- Tax: rev-share paid to US entities will be gross; for non-US recipients we require W-8/W-9 or local tax documentation before payment.

I'll attach a sample payout schedule PDF to the contract bundle for procurement (Referral_Pricing_Schedule.pdf).

-ben
